title: Set up SSH for the portfolio
prompt: You've decided to push the portfolio over SSH. Put the setup steps in the order that works, from no key at all to a successful `git push` over SSH. Finish all the local key work (create the key, load it into the agent) before you touch GitHub, and prove SSH works before you change the repository.
hints: You can't add or copy a key that doesn't exist yet.
GitHub must know your public key before the connection test can greet you.
Changing the remote URL is the last step, once you know SSH works.
explanation: First generate the pair with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`, then load the private key into the agent so you don't retype the passphrase. Copy the public key (the `.pub` file) and add it to your GitHub account. `ssh -T git@github.com` proves the setup works before you change anything in the repository. Finally, `git remote set-url` switches `origin` to the SSH URL so Git uses the key on the next push.

items.keygen: Run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "maya.okafor@example.com"` and set a passphrase.
items.github: On GitHub, open Settings, SSH and GPG keys, New SSH key, and paste it.
items.test: Run `ssh -T git@github.com` and check it greets you by username.
items.seturl: Run `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:maya-okafor/portfolio.git`, then `git push`.
